summary: On the first day of Herzog's consultations, Religious Zionism and Shas recommended Netanyahu, while Yisrael Beiteinu recommended Eisenkot and ruled out a government relying on Arab parties. UTJ's Degel HaTorah faction confirmed on its rabbis' instructions that it will not recommend anyone, and the stance of UTJ's Agudat Yisrael MKs remains unclear. Ra'am says it will recommend Eisenkot, and Joint List MK Ofer Cassif told Anadolu his alliance would likely do the same, so the Times of Israel reports Eisenkot is expected to get the first shot at forming a government. The remaining parties meet Herzog on Thursday, ending with Likud, and neither candidate yet has a clear path to a majority.

phase.now: Herzog's consultations resume on Nov 5: UTJ at 8:30 a.m., then the remaining parties, with Likud last
phase.next: Herzog chooses a candidate for the mandate (legal deadline Nov 11); the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he wants Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism in any future government and that the public does not want one dependent on Ra'am and the Joint List. Without a majority, he needs defectors or a new partner from the other side.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu and says he won't sit with him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president. Ynet reports Joint List and Ra'am leaders met in Nazareth on Nov 2 and will coordinate their recommendations. Ynet reports Bennett sides with Liberman against a government relying on Arab parties, believing it would collapse. On Nov 3 Golan met Joint List leaders and they agreed to keep coordinating, while the Times of Israel notes the bloc's joint statement gave no indication of how it would govern without Arab parties. On Nov 4 Ra'am announced it will recommend Eisenkot, while Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog a government cannot be formed with Arab parties.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. Unnamed sources tell Ynet that Liberman berated Eisenkot at a Saturday meeting, saying the minority-government push hurt the bloc.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am and said on Nov 2 he would oppose an Eisenkot minority government.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out. Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party might back an Eisenkot government from outside without a draft law first, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 2 Liberman declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ, saying the bloc will have to see what happens. Ynet reports on Nov 3 that Eisenkot is focusing on courting the Haredi parties and that Liberman has left the door open to talks on including them. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 3 that Shas and UTJ stress no decision has been made, with their rabbis due back around the start of consultations. On Nov 4 Shas recommended Netanyahu, and Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it would not compromise key priorities to bring Haredi parties in, Ynet reports.

blockers.text: Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman pledged not to sit with Shas and UTJ, though on Nov 2 he declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.
Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it rejects compromising security and economic priorities to include Haredi parties.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ. Kan cites Netanyahu associate Benny Biton as saying Netanyahu wants unity, and an unnamed Likud official named Herzog and Trump as guarantors for Eisenkot. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point. Likud whip Ofir Katz told Army Radio the party opposes rotation and others can join the existing coalition. Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu has given up on unity talks and is preparing for a new election. Ynet reports Netanyahu told associates privately he is not ruling out any option, including rotation, and that Katz says unity is off if the opposition ousts Speaker Ohana. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he is open to a broad government with any party that does not support terrorism but that he should lead it; an associate told Ynet no unity proposal has yet been made. Israel Hayom reports a Likud source's assessment, not a negotiated offer, that Netanyahu could accept unity if he served about two years and then became president, with Eisenkot taking over.

blockers.text: Likud whip Ofir Katz said the party opposes a rotation of the premiership.
Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: In his first public remarks since election night, Netanyahu said on Nov 2 he should lead any government, wants to keep Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, and is open to a broad government with parties that don't support terrorism.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: Eisenkot completed a first round of coalition talks with Together, the Democrats and Yisrael Beiteinu, aiming for a national emergency government, Ynet reports.
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: Bennett said on Nov 3 his whole party will work to help Eisenkot form a government and urged quickly replacing Speaker Ohana; Ynet reports he opposes a government relying on Arab parties.
red_lines: No government reliant on Arab parties (per Ynet)

אמת.stance: Golan met Joint List leaders Jabareen and Tibi on Nov 3, and the two sides agreed to keep coordinating toward a change government.

ל.stance: At Yisrael Beiteinu's Nov 4 consultation, MK Oded Forer recommended Eisenkot as most likely to form a government, ruled out relying on Arab parties, and rejected security or economic concessions to bring in Haredi parties.

שס.stance: At its Nov 4 consultation Shas recommended Netanyahu, with MK Malkieli voicing hope for a coalition of at least 61 and saying the Council of Torah Sages fully backs Deri.

ג.stance: Degel HaTorah, with four of UTJ's seven MKs, said it will not recommend any candidate on the instructions of Rabbis Lando and Hirsch; Agudat Yisrael's three MKs have not said whether they will back Netanyahu.

ב.stance: Otzma Yehudit confirmed to Fox News Digital on Nov 3 that it will recommend Netanyahu to Herzog.

ט.stance: Religious Zionism recommended Netanyahu on Nov 4, with its delegation arguing Arab nationalist parties are not legitimate partners in forming a government, Ynet reports.

עם.stance: Ra'am announced it will recommend Eisenkot to Herzog, Ynet reports.

ודם.stance: MK Ofer Cassif told Anadolu the Joint List would likely recommend Eisenkot when it meets Herzog on Thursday, though it was still discussing its position.

timeline.text: Al Jazeera, citing Channel 12, reports the Joint List is expected to coordinate with Eisenkot, endorsing him if asked or abstaining if he prefers.
Cassif told Anadolu the Joint List would likely recommend Eisenkot at its Thursday meeting with Herzog but was still deliberating.
The Times of Israel reports Eisenkot is expected to receive the mandate after Ra'am confirmed its endorsement, with consultations resuming Thursday morning.
UTJ's Degel HaTorah faction confirmed it will not recommend any candidate, following its rabbis' instructions; Agudat Yisrael's position is unclear.
Yisrael Beiteinu formally recommended Eisenkot to Herzog and ruled out a government relying on Arab parties, though it allows cooperation on single bills.
Ra'am announced it will recommend Eisenkot for the mandate, Ynet reports.
Eisenkot's party finished a first round of coalition talks with Together, the Democrats and Yisrael Beiteinu toward a national emergency government.
Shas recommended Netanyahu and hoped for a coalition of at least 61; Herzog asked the delegation why it was not pushing for unity.
Zehut's Feiglin said he will recommend Netanyahu but questioned the result's legitimacy and called for another election.
Religious Zionism recommended Netanyahu, and its delegates argued Arab nationalist parties should not help form a government or replace the Speaker.
Herzog wrapped up his consultation with Religious Zionism and began meeting Shas, both of which back Netanyahu.
Herzog suggested that a far-right minister's opposition to including Arab parties is racist, the Times of Israel reports.
Herzog told factions that, to avoid another election, they must accept that not every campaign commitment can be fulfilled.
The election committee certified the results, saying it found no irregularities or evidence that the outcome was altered; Likud and Shas abstained in the presidium vote.
Receiving the official results, Herzog said the elections are over and it is time to face reality.
An unnamed Joint List source told Fox News the alliance is likely to endorse Eisenkot.
Says Netanyahu lacks a majority and that the opposition bloc will form the next government, the Jerusalem Post reports.
Ahead of the consultations, Ynet projects Eisenkot is poised to receive more recommendations than Netanyahu.
The attorney general asked the Shin Bet to report on its probe into Arab parties' alleged electoral fraud, saying no evidence had yet been submitted, AFP reports.
Herzog's office says he will start with smaller parties to hear all views and may hold further rounds of consultations before choosing a candidate.
Joint List leader Jabareen says the opposition must accept political reality and join forces with Arab parties to remove Netanyahu, AFP reports.
Haaretz's live coverage reports Likud is weighing whether to refuse to recognize the election results.
Anadolu reports Shas will recommend Netanyahu to form the next government.
After their meeting, Eisenkot and the other opposition leaders vow to form an emergency government as soon as possible, the Jerusalem Post reports.
Announces it will recommend Netanyahu to Herzog and call on left-wing parties to end boycotts and join a broad Jewish government.
The Zehut chair says he will also recommend Netanyahu but ask Herzog to push for new elections, claiming the vote's integrity was compromised.
The party's Council of Torah Sages backs recommending Netanyahu after his commitment on yeshiva students' status, Israel National News reports.
Eisenkot, Bennett, Golan and Liberman agree to launch coalition talks immediately and reaffirm backing Eisenkot for the first mandate.
Channel 12 reports the leaders discussed backing Lapid for Knesset speaker and will decide by Monday.
Says his party will mobilize all its efforts to help Eisenkot form a government and urges quickly replacing Speaker Ohana.
